utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-98-32-A, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vasiljevic, you are in court and can you hear me? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I take it you can hear me in a language that you can understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Then may I have the appearances in this case. First, the appellant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your Honour, Vladimir Domazet, lead counsel for the appellant. And on my left side is Mr. Knoops, my Dutch lawyer and my legal consultant and maybe a future co-counsel in this case. He was working also on the Defence appeal brief. And I respectively ask Your Honour if he can assist me on this Status Conference today here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, may I ask one question: You have described Mr. Knoops as counsel. Do I take it that he is a member of the Dutch bar?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, then, Mr. Domazet, without setting a precedent, I will for this particular case allow the motion. Therefore, Mr. Knoops will be admitted as consultant to sit with you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, my name is Christopher Staker. I appear with my colleague Stefan Wirth. Our case manager is Ms. Lourdes Galicia. On a personal note, Your Honour, I would just add that at the end of this week I will be leaving my position as senior appeals counsel in the Office of the Prosecutor, and this is, therefore, my last appearance before the Tribunal in that capacity. And it's a pleasure for me that this last appearance should be before Your Honour, Judge Shahabuddeen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Staker, we will move around professionally. I'm sure Mr. Domazet will agree to that. I take it you are leaving for greener pastures. You then only have my admiration and good wishes for the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, we are dealing with this case which is before us pursuant to a scheduling order made by me on the 4th of August this year, setting today as the day for a second Status Conference in this case. The circumstances in which this date was prescribed have been set out in the scheduling order. Now, the last Status Conference was on the 17th of March, and so we are about one week outside of the prescribed time, but the circumstances in which that was overlooked have been referred to in today's scheduling order. Now, the judgment in this case was rendered on 29th of November. The notice of appeal was filed on the 30th of December, 2002. And there was an amended notice of appeal on 12 February 2002. So the applicant in this case is clearly an appellant, and therefore Rule 65 bis (B) applies, as we all know that rule which has been previously read out by me in March this year to the accused, the appellant, requires that a Status Conference be held every 120 days. The object is to allow the parties in question to raise any issues in relation to the appeal, including his mental or physical condition. So now first, I turn to the appellant, and/or to his counsel, and I ask whether they need to make any representations about the conditions of detention or about the conditions of the appellant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, the appellant has no problem, any physical or mental problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then, may I refer to the status of the appeal. As I understand it, the pleading process has been completed. We've had a brief by the appellant and response by the Prosecution. Yesterday, I think two documents were filed by the appellant, one being his reply to the Prosecution's response and another document supporting the first document, I think. So now, is there any representation that the appellant or his counsel might need to make so far as the status of the appeal is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, the Court has before it a Rule 115 motion by the appellant. It is proposed to deal with that shortly, and then the President will fix a time for the hearing of the appeal proper and we will proceed that way. Is there anything you have to say, Mr. Staker?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would simply note that the Prosecution is at the stage of completing a disclosure review. It is expected that will be completed within a matter of days. Any disclosure material that may arise out of that exercise, we expect will be minimal, if any. As I say, in a matter of days, but that's perhaps one last fact to be taken into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Staker, this disclosure, does this disclosure exercise arise out of the Rule 115 motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It is a review of material coming into possession of the Office of the Prosecutor since the trial phase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: It is automatic then?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: It is automatic. Disclosure is a continued --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then in that sense, I'm sure the appellant will appreciate the work you propose to undertake or are undertaking at this moment. Is that right, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You look forward to the completion of the task on which the Prosecution is engaged. Well, then, are there any other matters which we might need to discuss at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Not on the side of the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Not at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: On that note, we will take the adjournment, just remarking how useful it is really for the Court to be in constant and regular touch with the appellant and not allow him to languish in detention unnecessarily, without the possibility of seeing the court in session. Thank you very much.
